title: Reuse existing enterprise Wi-Fi profiles on reconnect
head: 1bcaf6bee339
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A failed profile enumeration or per-profile read is treated as no existing enterprise profile
leads.consequence: If connection show transiently returns nonzero, the process substitution and candidate reads hide the error; the helper proceeds to nmcli connection add. If that later command succeeds, it creates and activates a minimal PEAP/MSCHAPv2 profile rather than the existing CA/domain-constrained UUID. An add failure instead exits with no fallback; no existing profile is deleted. The next attempt may reuse the existing profile or the newly created one depending on list order. Check list/read statuses and fail closed instead of treating errors as an empty inventory.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus Q2 confirmed, very low likelihood; not published

leads.summary: First matching UUID is not the profile selected by Quickshell for this SSID
leads.consequence: With two wpa-eap profiles for eduroam (different institutional settings or accounts), nmcli's default list order is active, then profile name/path; the helper edits and activates the first. Quickshell's reference profile instead prefers active then most recent successful timestamp. When those differ, submitted identity/password overwrite the wrong stored institutional profile, leave the intended profile untouched, and can connect under the wrong CA/domain policy or fail. Choose the exact profile the UI would activate, or explicitly disambiguate. The single-profile test does not detect this.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus Q1 confirmed, low severity, no worse than base; not published

leads.summary: Trailing linefeed in a valid Wi-Fi SSID still bypasses profile reuse
leads.consequence: -e no fixes colon/backslash escaping, but for a name ending in LF the nmcli value is printable raw text and Bash $(...) strips trailing LF, so the SSID differs from the Quickshell name. The helper creates a minimal profile instead of reusing the institutional one, with the same loss of CA/domain restrictions as the original bug for this narrower input. The code does not delete the old UUID; the new profile persists if activation succeeds. Preserve the final newline via a sentinel or compare SSID bytes rather than command-substitution text.

leads.summary: Reused legacy EAP profiles retain the old eight-second authentication timeout
leads.consequence: New profiles now set 802-1x.auth-timeout 0, but users who previously connected through Omarchy may already have a stored eight-second profile. Reuse edits only identity and password, leaving timeout at 8; slow RADIUS handshakes continue to abort on upgrade and reconnection. Open, non-stacked #12279 includes a migration that resets old wpa-eap timeout 8 to 0. Coordinate its migration when resolving the Model.js merge conflict; do not discard it by accepting this PR's helper hunk alone.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified; published as Related note

leads.summary: Enterprise reuse fixture passes even when the save operation is omitted
leads.consequence: The mock writes profile values immediately on each set and ignores save/quit. Real nmcli connection edit changes its local copy and commits only on save. Removing the production save line lets all six regression checks pass while the profile is not persisted for later activation/reuse. Make the mock stage changes until save and assert persisted identity/password, including when save fails.
leads.triage: factual (test fidelity); verified from mock source; not published

leads.summary: Related panel PRs overlap the enterprise failure reason and one repairs a missing retry prompt
leads.consequence: #10602 moves reprompt into panel before refresh, addressing a reproduced vanished-delegate failure; this PR still calls refresh in failNetworkAction before the delegate calls openPasswordPrompt. Both #10602 and #13088 alter the exact failureReason call, and each alternative branch omits the new isEnterpriseSecurity argument. Three-way merges have conflict markers in failNetworkAction (and #10602 network test); resolving either by taking the other branch can silently restore Wrong password for enterprise timeouts or lose the recovery fix. Preserve both the enterprise flag and panel-owned reprompt when combining. #10602 mergeability UNKNOWN, #13088 MERGEABLE versus base, neither stacked with this PR.

limits: Sandbox uses a synthetic nmcli stub, not a real NetworkManager daemon; H1/H2/H3 outcomes are conditional on the modeled outputs and the shipped 1.58.1 source. No live QML render was attempted because the brief did not reserve a desktop slot.

The package list specifies networkmanager and quickshell without exact pinned package revisions. Dependency source consulted: NetworkManager 1.58.1, Quickshell released v0.3.1 (and 2026-09-22 source tree); applicability should be checked against deployed packages.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12889#issuecomment-5775621077) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12889#issuecomment-5841759038), checked at `1bcaf6bee339`. Both earlier findings are resolved. The retry-text change adds one small new wording issue, and one untested hypothesis about reusing CAT-installed profiles is noted below.

| Earlier finding | Status at `1bcaf6bee339` |
|---|---|
| Escaped SSIDs bypass the existing enterprise profile | Resolved |
| Inline retry prompt hard-codes "Wrong password" | Resolved (source-traced and simulated, no live UI) |

**Verified:** [Model.js:344](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/1bcaf6bee339e650bcda814b333e6a6adc28ec8b/shell/plugins/panels/network/Model.js#L344) now reads the SSID with `nmcli -e no -g`. Real nmcli 1.58.1 read synthetic profiles, with writes and activation stubbed:

```text
Requested SSID   Previous head (d3c34d36)             Current head
Campus:Secure    new profile created                  existing UUID
Campus\Secure    new profile created                  existing UUID
Lab\:Net         edited the Lab:Net profile instead   existing UUID
eduroam          existing UUID                        existing UUID
```

The new mock reproduces nmcli's default escaping byte for byte, and the new colon case fails against the previous `Model.js`. Both head network test scripts pass.

**Verified:** in the inline retry prompt ([Panel.qml:2032](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/1bcaf6bee339e650bcda814b333e6a6adc28ec8b/shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml#L2032)), an enterprise `WifiAuthTimeout` now reads "Connection timed out", and a PSK `WifiAuthTimeout` still reads "Wrong password". Other failures after a submitted passphrase now show their mapped reason (for example "Connection failed" or "Network lost") or the panel's own "Timed out connecting" after its 30 s timer, instead of "Wrong password".

## New: a `NoSecrets` retry now reads "Passphrase required"

A simulation built from the source, using each revision's `Model.js` and inline-text expression, shows:

```text
Failure after a submitted passphrase   Before 1bcaf6be    Current head
NoSecrets (PSK or enterprise)          Wrong password     Passphrase required
WifiAuthTimeout (PSK)                  Wrong password     Wrong password
```

Quickshell 0.3.1 documents `NoSecrets` as the signal for a wrong PSK (`src/network/wifi.hpp:30-31`). In the NetworkManager 1.58.1 source, a PSK mismatch leads to a secrets request that fails with `NO_SECRETS` when no secret agent answers, and Omarchy ships none. The comment at [Panel.qml:997-1002](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/1bcaf6bee339e650bcda814b333e6a6adc28ec8b/shell/plugins/panels/network/Panel.qml#L997-L1002) says a wrong saved PSK fails with `WifiAuthTimeout` instead, and the runtime reason was not observed here. The change follows the earlier review's suggestion, which considered timeouts but not `NoSecrets`.

**Impact:** when a typed passphrase is wrong and the failure arrives as `NoSecrets`, the reopened prompt says "Passphrase required" instead of "Wrong password". From the same NetworkManager source, failed secured enterprise activations also appear to end as `NO_SECRETS` rather than a timeout, so the new "Connection timed out" text may rarely appear (unverified).

**Suggested change:** keep "Wrong password" for a `NoSecrets` reprompt right after a submitted passphrase, or limit the mapped inline text to the enterprise timeout (this second option would also drop the other mapped reasons shown above). A test pinning the inline text for `NoSecrets` would cover it.

## Hypothesis: reused CAT profiles may not receive the typed password

This is source-only and was not tested at runtime. It concerns the profile reuse from the first commit. The PR's unchecked CAT test plan item could settle it if run without a secret agent and with credentials known to work.

```text
CAT PEAP/TTLS profile: 802-1x.password-flags=1 (agent-owned)
  helper writes password via `connection edit`  -> cached, not persisted
  activation asks secret agents for it          -> only nmcli's own agent, which declines
  activation fails: no-secrets -> prompt reopens -> repeats
```

The GÉANT CAT Linux installer stores the PEAP/TTLS password as agent-owned. In the NetworkManager 1.58.1 source, activation asks a secret agent for agent-owned secrets. Omarchy ships no agent, and `nmcli connection up` without `--ask` declines the request. If this holds, on a system with no secret agent, reusing a CAT PEAP/TTLS profile fails on every attempt. The base code instead created a separate CA-less profile that could connect.

**What would settle it:** on a system with no secret agent running, submit credentials known to work for a CAT-installed PEAP/TTLS profile. A `no-secrets` failure alone does not distinguish this from a wrong password; the NetworkManager log line `has security, but secrets are required` with no association attempt, or a stored profile file without a `password=` entry after the helper runs, would. Untested remedies: pass the password to activation through nmcli's `passwd-file` (without putting it in argv or a file on disk), or set `802-1x.password-flags 0` on reuse (this changes the institution profile's secret storage).

**Related:** enterprise profiles created by the earlier panel code keep `802-1x.auth-timeout 8` when this PR reuses them. Open #12279 adds a migration that resets them to 0, and its `Model.js` hunk overlaps this PR's.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** previous-head and head test scripts, including the head tests against the previous `Model.js` and `Panel.qml`; real nmcli 1.58.1 output formatting against synthetic profiles on a private mock bus, with writes and activation stubbed; a source-derived simulation of the retry prompt; and NetworkManager 1.58.1, Quickshell 0.3.1 and CAT installer source. No live QML rendering, Wi-Fi hardware, RADIUS server, secret agent or real NetworkManager daemon was exercised.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
